capture_engagement.description: Deprecated: use `tracking.engagement`. Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email your code rendered are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A send with `tracking` can't also carry this field. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured under. Defaults to the recipient's email address. The events join the person who has this ID, or start a new person when nobody has it, so pass the ID your app uses for this recipient to see the email on their person. No events are captured when the project's engagement events setting is off or when tracking turns engagement off for this send. The email goes out either way.

from.description: Sender of the email your code rendered, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, the email goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default. A project with no verified sending domain can send from the PostHog test sender only when PostHog offers that sender to its organization, and then only to members of the organization. That sender ignores this field and says so in the response's `warnings`.

html.description: HTML body of the email, exactly as the recipient should see it. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB, and quotes and line breaks count twice. A larger email can't be sent here.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email your code rendered go to. The PostHog test sender ignores them and says so in the response's `warnings`.

sensitive.description: Mark the email as sensitive when it carries login links, reset tokens, or codes. Sensitive emails leave the subject off engagement events, record only the site address of a clicked link, and keep the content out of logs. They are tracked like any other email unless `tracking` turns tracking off. Defaults to the matched template's setting, or true when no template matches. It can't be false when the matched template is sensitive.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only, at most 256 characters. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Without it, PostHog derives the text from html. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB.

clicks.description: Whether the email's links go through a redirect that counts clicks. Defaults to true, for sensitive emails too. Needs `opens`. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address.

engagement.description: Whether the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true.

opens.description: Whether PostHog adds its open pixel to the email. Defaults to true.

tracking.description: What PostHog tracks for the email your code rendered. `true` tracks opens and clicks and captures engagement events. `false` turns off all of it, now and for any kind of tracking added later. An object sets each kind on its own, and a kind it leaves out keeps its default. Without this field, PostHog tracks opens and clicks and captures engagement events, for sensitive emails too. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address, so an app link still opens the app. Click tracking needs open tracking. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says. The object form needs a JSON body.
